column4: staging refuses reason=policy-loaded before this when Android's policy is loaded host-wide, and copy_tree takes this plain copy only when /proc/self/attr/current shows no policy at all (a host with its own policy stages through stage-gsi-labeled), so it runs with no SELinux policy loaded, where cp -a carries the image's labels, owners and modes whole

text of rhizo-final-cleanup.service's ExecStart, which runs on the boot after the uninstall took the GRUB drop-in and rhizo-policy.service away, so no policy is loaded; it strips only a label still reading exactly rhizo_host_exec
text of rhizo-final-cleanup.service's module-tree ExecStart, run on the next boot with no policy loaded; it strips only a label still reading exactly rhizo_host_module_file

selinux_xattr_report clear: under a loaded policy the kernel refuses it, the report exits 1, and step 4 sets XATTRS_DEFERRED and schedules the same strip in rhizo-final-cleanup.service for the next boot, which loads no policy
selinux_xattr_report clear's module-tree strip: refused under a loaded policy, which exits 1 and defers it to rhizo-final-cleanup.service on the next boot with no policy loaded
the primer's label_write(): refuses a read-only or GSI-backed inode, and its _RELABEL_SPEC destinations are held to relabelto grants by relabel-spec.py
_stage_tethering_apex labels the apex copy it just staged system_file, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type
_stage_decompressed_apexes labels each payload it just extracted system_file, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type

_relabel_prepared_vendor labels the prepared vendor tree's bin/lib files; rhizo_host holds relabelfrom and relabelto on vendor_file_type (rhizo-policy.cil) and a refusal fails prepare-tree; on a host with its own policy it runs in a child SELinux namespace holding Android's compiled policy (prepare_tree_verb)
label_write(): the one writer every tree-walking relabel pass goes through, refusing a read-only or GSI-backed inode (relabel-scope.py)
label_host_binaries stamps rhizo_host_exec, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type, on host entrypoints that are unlabeled (relabelfrom granted); already-labeled files are skipped and a refusal is logged
label_host_modules stamps rhizo_host_module_file, on which rhizo_host holds relabelfrom and relabelto; each refusal is collected and reported

label_before_policy: every caller labels a file or node the stager just created on the sandbox tmpfs or flat tree (flat and apex dirs system_file, /dev nodes, dma_heap, dri, tun, the enforce shadow, sysctl and sysrq shadows), each a rhizo_relabel_dest_file or rhizo_relabel_dest_dev type; in an unshared namespace with no policy yet it writes nothing and Android labels them after its load
_build_flat_trees labels the flat directory it just made on the sandbox tmpfs system_file, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type
_build_flat_trees labels the apex bind target it just made in the flat apex dir with the label the GSI's own apex carries
_build_flat_trees labels the flat apex dir it just made system_file, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type
_stage_node labels the device node it just made under the sandbox /dev with its plat_file_contexts label, a rhizo_relabel_dest_dev type
the stager labels the /dev/dma_heap dir it just made dmabuf_heap_device, a rhizo_relabel_dest_dev type
the root build labels the dri nodes it just made gpu_device, as plat_file_contexts does, a rhizo_relabel_dest_dev type
the root build labels the /dev/tun node it just made tun_device, a rhizo_relabel_dest_dev type
the root build labels the decoy enforce file it just made on its own tmpfs rhizo_enforce_shadow
stage_sysctl_shadows labels each shadow file it just made on the sandbox /dev tmpfs as the real sysctl node
stage_sysctl_shadows labels the sysrq sink it just made on the sandbox /dev tmpfs as /proc/sysrq-trigger
_mask_sysrq_trigger labels the sysrq sink it just made, when missing or mislabeled, as the node it masks
harden_proc_sys labels each shadow file it just made on the sandbox tmpfs as the real /proc/sys node it shadows

bind_decoy_enforce labels the decoy enforce file it just created on its own scratch tmpfs rhizo_enforce_shadow, in Android's fresh SELinux namespace, unshared before it by gg's root build or the handoff joiner's pid 1, which has no policy loaded yet, and namespace mode loads none on the host; a refusal is caught and logged

NodeFd.setxattr: the namespace-mode input label service writes hidraw_device on a /dev/hidraw node through its /proc/self/fd link, running as rhizo_input_label in Android's SELinux namespace with relabelfrom on device and relabelto on hidraw_device alone (selinux_policy.NAMESPACE_LABEL_SERVICE), and set_xattr_through_fd refuses an fd whose dev, inode and rdev differ from the node asked for, before and after the write

stage_gsi_labeled copies the GSI's own read-only image after unsharing a child SELinux namespace and loading Android's compiled policy into it, so the image's labels are valid where cp -a reads and writes them; the host's policy still checks each write as an ancestor (relabelfrom on the new file's host label, relabelto and associate on unlabeled_t)
labels the tmpfs net.core file it just wrote in the sandbox proc_net or proc_bpf, both rhizo_relabel_dest_file types; a refusal is logged
labels the sandbox's own tmpfs net.core directory proc_net, a rhizo_relabel_dest_file type; a refusal is logged

labels a payload it just wrote into the template image it built staging_data_file, on which rhizo_host holds relabelto; prepare runs it before Android's policy enforces; on a host with its own policy it runs in a child SELinux namespace holding Android's compiled policy (data-template.sh, launcher3.py in-android-policy)

labels a directory of the template image it built apex_data_file, on which rhizo_host holds relabelto; prepare runs it before Android's policy enforces; on a host with its own policy it runs in a child SELinux namespace holding Android's compiled policy (data-template.sh, launcher3.py in-android-policy)

runs as the new account itself (rhizo-user-prep@.service's User=%i line, never root), copying /etc/skel into its own empty home; mode and timestamps on files it owns need no capability, and no owner, ACL or label is carried

runs as the VT's owner from /etc/profile.d/rhizo-console-vt.sh, never root, and writes only the POSIX ACL of a node it owns, which needs no capability; rhizo_host holds setattr on rhizo_host_device, the VT's type

runs as root from rhizo-session-vt@.service, before a login session's scope starts, on the VT logind names for that session (grant_session refuses anything but a char node 4:1..63), and writes only its POSIX ACL: a user:0 entry and the mask; rhizo_host holds fowner and setattr on rhizo_host_device, the VT's type

runs as the directory's owner from rhizo-deskd.service's ExecStartPre= and rhizo-user-prep@.service, never root, and writes only the POSIX ACL of a directory it owns: a user:0 rwx or --x entry and the mask, which needs no capability; the directory is PID 1's post-policy RuntimeDirectory=, type rhizo_host, on which rhizo_host holds setattr

label_android_file: a file the CLI creates in Android's data has no Android label until this write; it runs host-side only on a host that loaded no policy, where any owner may set a label and no policy check runs, and inside launcher3.py in-android-policy's namespace holding Android's policy on a host with its own; it labels only the inbox APK or device-state file the calling function just created, and reads the label back

label_android_file: the /data/media/0 mount point attach just created has no label until this write of media_rw_data_file, read back, and a failure removes the directory; attach makes it host-side only on a host that loaded no policy, and through label_in_policy_namespace's in-android-policy child on a host with its own

_stage_vendor_scaffold labels the device-state link it just made in the instance's own vendor staging tree vendor_configs_file, in host mode before any policy loads, when any owner may set a label and no policy check runs; in namespace mode the prelabel child labels it, and with a policy loaded the primer's walk does

label_in_namespace: in-android-policy's label and label-fd verbs write the one path or fd their root caller names, the inbox APK or device-state file it just made, only after the child unshares a namespace, loads Android's compiled policy and drops every capability; the label is printed back for the caller to compare

label_device_state_dir labels Rhizo's own device-state directory, refused unless a device-state name directly under the state root: the prelabel child calls it after it enters a namespace holding Android's policy, and host mode calls it only while no policy is loaded, when any owner may set a label

label_fd labels the inbox APK the broker or the CLI just created, through its fd: write_labeled runs it host-side only on a host that loaded no policy, where any owner may set a label and no policy check runs, and inside launcher3.py in-android-policy's namespace holding Android's policy on a host with its own; the label is read back before pm sees the file
